prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene, opening the field of moire flat-band quantum matter

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B021 as a single-part prize with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. The core of the case is unchanged and has not been seriously contested: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gives a quantitative, falsifiable prediction in which one twist angle quenches the kinetic energy so that interactions dominate, and the 2018 experiments confirmed correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle. In statistical-physics terms the twist angle is a new, continuously tunable knob on the ratio of interaction to bandwidth, which is why the idea generalised to a whole family of moire platforms rather than remaining a single material. The chair's summary shows that B021 is the only shortlisted achievement named as an alternative by five of the other members, so a citation limited to the flat-band prediction and the observed phases, without asserting a pairing mechanism, appears to be the version most colleagues can accept. I regard that wording as the honest scope of what has been established.
statement.case_against: The strongest objections stand and I weigh them as real. The microscopic origin of superconductivity and of the correlated states is unresolved, so the prize would reward a platform and its phenomenology, not a settled explanation. Eight years is short next to the fifteen years of stable interpretation behind B030 or the decade of multinational replication behind B024. Attribution is incomplete: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, and the independent groups of Dean, Young, Yazdani and Efetov are outside the credit, as is earlier moire band-structure work. Rapid growth of the literature is partly a sign of open questions, and I should not count it purely as merit.

responses.point: Kroll argues that breadth of follow-on activity in twisted bilayer graphene is not settled understanding, and that he could support B021 only if the citation rests on the flat-band prediction and observed correlated states, not on superconductivity; he also stresses that the B024 credit is clean and the 10^-18 result is mature.
responses.response: I accept the distinction and I have changed my wording because of it: my round-2 citation names the prediction and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states and claims no mechanism. I still hold that the field's growth reflects more than open questions, because the phenomenology (correlated insulators, superconducting domes, tunability by gate and angle) has been reproduced by several independent laboratories. On B024 I concede that the credit to Katori and Ye is the cleanest on the list and that maturity is not in doubt. My remaining difference is conceptual: a lattice clock sharpens a measurement that earlier prizes opened, whereas the twist angle opened a new class of tunable many-body states. I would still keep B024 as an alternative rather than rank it above B021.

responses.point: Pearce, the chair, replies that he cannot fully rebut the wider experimental credit for B030 but prefers Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, and that the 2016 prize did not cover time-reversal-invariant systems.
responses.response: The chair's argument about the 2016 prize is fair: the Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz citation concerned topological phase transitions and the integer quantum Hall state, and I withdraw the suggestion that it makes B030 ineligible in principle. I also now agree that Mele should not be replaced, since the Z2 classification and the graphene proposal were joint Kane-Mele work, so my opening preference for Hasan in his place no longer seems defensible on theory credit. That leaves B030 with the most defensible three names (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) but still with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan omissions in the background. I weigh that attribution cost somewhat above the attribution cost in B021, which is why B030 stays my first alternative and not my preferred configuration.

responses.point: Danielsson holds that B030 has been stable for nearly two decades, that Hasan's 3D work should be a distinct achievement rather than a substitute for Mele, and that B021's microscopic interpretation is less settled.
responses.response: I agree that the 3D work would have to be recognised as a separate achievement, and a two-part prize that carries it would exceed the three-person limit once Kane, Mele and Molenkamp are credited. On interpretation I concede the point: B030 is far more settled. But the question is what the prize recognises. The twisted bilayer case is a prediction followed by an observation of new phases, and that structure is independent of whether the pairing mechanism is eventually found. I would add that a mature prize is not automatically a better one when the discovery of the field is as recent as this one, and the committee can wait for B030 as easily as for B021.

responses.point: Olsson, who opened with two names for B021, moved to all three after round-1 discussion and rests the case on the interface and registry in the moire structure.
responses.response: I welcome the move to three names; it keeps the prediction anchored in Bistritzer's 2011 derivation of the magic angle, which a two-name credit would cut away. Her interface and registry emphasis is complementary to my tunable-interaction argument, since both say the twist angle is a new control parameter. The question she has not resolved, and I have not either, is Yuan Cao; I think the committee should state openly that the citation credits the prediction and the experimental group leadership and does not claim to cover every individual contribution.

uncertainties: Whether an eight-year-old experimental discovery with an unresolved pairing mechanism is mature enough, given that Kroll, Pearce, Lindroth and Danielsson all raise timing and I have no way to resolve it beyond the replication record.
Whether Yuan Cao, who is outside the credited names, should be reflected in the citation wording or a different three-person set, which I leave open.
Whether the committee would prefer a new-state-of-matter prize in B030 over B021 once the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan omissions are weighed; I regard it as a close second and would not oppose it.
Whether a two-part prize pairing B021 with B024 is feasible; I have not found a configuration that stays within three people across two parts, so I keep a single part.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict. My documented co-authors and institutions (Gothenburg, Max Planck institutes, Oxford, Freiburg) include none of the credited persons for B021, B030 or B024, and no member has raised a conflict that bears on my position.
